read: partial (the seminar concept note and registration notice; no proceedings or papers were found)
what_they_did: The Archaeological Survey of India announced a seminar on the decipherment of the Indus script and invited papers.
The registration notice set a deadline of 30 June 2025 (notice 772).
what_they_found: The concept note states that the script has over 400 principal signs and is hypothesised to be logo-syllabic (concept note).
It says most scholars agree it was written right to left and that stroke signs are numerals (concept note).
It names the lack of a bilingual text, the short texts and the small number of specimens as the main obstacles (concept note).
It says the proceedings of the seminar are anticipated, but none were found online.
strength_and_limits: The note is a call for papers, not research, and gives no data or method.
Without proceedings there is nothing to test yet.

authors_next.idea: Publish the proceedings of the seminar.

ideas_for_us.idea: Offer a frozen hidden-sign test for any reading presented at the seminar: a proposer commits to sign values, we mask signs in held-out, family-clean texts, and the reading must predict them better than a trigram.
ideas_for_us.why: It gives claimed decipherments one shared, falsifiable score instead of case-by-case argument.
ideas_for_us.data_needed: M77 family-clean held-out split and the proposer's sign values.

ideas_for_us.idea: Test the concept note's consensus claims on M77: run the right-to-left direction check and the stroke-numeral check on family-clean texts and report how strong each is.
ideas_for_us.why: These are the shared starting points of most readings, so their strength should be measured, not assumed.
ideas_for_us.data_needed: M77 texts with line direction notes and stroke sign classes.
